clue.text: Early impression reader may be required to correct

definitions.text: Early impression reader may be required to correct

parts.words: Early impression reader may be required to correct
parts.note: a first printed copy of typeset text, which a proofreader checks and marks up before the final print run

explanation.surface: Someone's first impression of a person may need correcting later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early impression' sounds like a first opinion of someone, but it means a first printing, and the 'reader' is a proofreader.
explanation.definitionFit: A printer's trial sheet, pulled from type in a long tray, is checked for errors before publication.

clue.text: Georgia and Edgar arranged to have the car housed

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: the letters of the name Edgar are rearranged, as if put in a new order

explanation.surface: Georgia and Edgar sort out somewhere to keep their car.
explanation.definitionFit: A car kept indoors in its own shed has been put away under cover.

clue.text: The French girl, some say, appointed by law

parts.note: LE is the French masculine word for 'the'
GAL is a colloquial way some people pronounce and write 'girl'

explanation.surface: A French girl is officially appointed under the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fixed or authorised by statute is lawful.

clue.text: It is complicated to work out

definitions.meaning: a verb: to develop a plan in detail

explanation.surface: Solving this one is a complicated business.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means intricate; as a verb it means to develop a plan in fuller detail.

clue.text: Support for quiet ending

parts.note: PRO means in favour of, as in pros and cons
P, the musical abbreviation for piano or quiet, comes as the ending

explanation.surface: Someone backs a call for a quiet finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is a post or brace that holds something up.

clue.text: You won't be travelling this way in the main

definitions.text: You won't be travelling this way in the main

parts.words: You won't be travelling this way in the main
parts.note: 'the main' is a poetic name for the open sea, so this route is the one across land rather than by ship

explanation.surface: A remark that this route is not the usual one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly', but it is the main meaning the high seas.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey made by road or across country rather than by sea.

clue.text: Not a purpose-built building

parts.note: an ornamental structure in a park or garden, built for show and serving no real use

explanation.surface: A remark that some building was converted rather than designed for its job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purpose-built' suggests a converted building, but the point is a building with no purpose at all; British country estates often have one.
explanation.definitionFit: An extravagant ornamental tower or mock ruin built purely for decoration on an estate.

clue.text: Bird with golden talon broken

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: the letters are smashed up and put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A bird of prey's gilded claw has been broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A small European bunting, famously eaten as a delicacy in France.

clue.text: Herb finds many in Iowa church

parts.note: basil is a common kitchen herb

indicators.note: the letter for many is placed inside the abbreviation for Iowa

parts.note: IA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Iowa
C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many

explanation.surface: A herb is found in great quantity at a church in Iowa.
explanation.definitionFit: A large oblong Roman Catholic church given special ceremonial privileges by the Pope.

clue.text: A girl more confused by the rambling account

indicators.note: the letters of these three words are muddled into a different order

explanation.surface: A girl grows more confused by a long-winded story.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, rambling and confusing story or procedure is a tedious palaver.

clue.text: The continental industrialist had an inclination

parts.note: LE is 'the' in French, a continental language
an ant is proverbially industrious, so a playful name for one

explanation.surface: A European captain of industry had a leaning towards something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Industrialist' suggests a factory owner, but it is the hard-working ant.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of lean: tilted or was disposed towards something.

clue.text: Measure everything in turn by name

indicators.note: the word for everything is placed inside the word for turn

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone takes stock of everything, one by one, by name.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of liquid volume, eight pints.

clue.text: Theatrical account?

parts.note: a bill is an account to be paid, but in the theatre it is the poster advertising a show

explanation.surface: A dramatic telling of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Account' looks like a narrative or an invoice; here a bill is the poster announcing a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: A poster or programme announcing a theatre production and its cast.

clue.text: Gloomy lads I am shortly up setting

indicators.note: read as one word, upsetting, these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: I'M is the short form of 'I am'

explanation.surface: Gloomy lads are upsetting me, I am about to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary and depressing, like a cheerless rainy day.

clue.text: Inadequate supply leaves its mark on the town

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: to scar is to leave a lasting mark
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A shortage leaves its mark on a town.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth or shortage of something needed.

clue.text: Idleness indeed

definitions.meaning: split as in deed, this means engaged in actual doing

explanation.surface: A remark that laziness is real enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indeed' looks like an emphatic tag, but split as 'in deed' it means busy doing, the opposite of the first definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia or lack of activity; split in two it means busy doing.

clue.text: Harmonious character

definitions.meaning: agreeing or in accord, especially in music
a letter of the alphabet other than a vowel

explanation.surface: Describing someone of a pleasant, agreeable disposition.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means agreeing in sound; as a noun it is a letter that is not a vowel.

clue.text: Fellow worker covers a very large area with free musical composition

indicators.note: in a down clue, the fellow worker sits above and so covers the area

parts.note: the worker ant is a classic crossword worker
Asia is the largest continent

explanation.surface: A colleague takes charge of a huge territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of music written in free form, following the composer's fancy rather than a set structure.

clue.text: Father in twisted braces' put down by a typist

indicators.note: the word for father goes inside the jumbled letters
the letters of braces are twisted out of shape into a new order

parts.note: PA is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad, in twisted braces, is sat down by a secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' suggests rudeness, but it means pressed down on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The long key at the bottom of a keyboard that typists press to leave a gap between words.

clue.text: Try to do business with lots wandering round here in France

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the French word
the letters of lots wander into a new order

parts.note: ICI is French for here

explanation.surface: Street traders roam about here in France, touting for custom.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask for or seek trade, custom or business.

clue.text: It is fashionable to come ashore well away from thesea!

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
to land is to come ashore from a boat

explanation.surface: It is trendy to disembark far from the coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Situated in the interior of a country, far from the coast.

clue.text: Be entitled to have the comic verse after the editor has returned

indicators.note: the rearranged verse follows the returned editor
the editor comes back, so its letters run the other way
comic suggests a funny mix-up of the letters of verse

explanation.surface: A writer earns a right to have funny verse printed once the editor is back.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit or be worthy of something.

clue.text: Tear net-like fabric with speed

parts.note: lace is an openwork fabric like net
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: Someone rips a delicate net fabric in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip or gash flesh or material jaggedly.

clue.text: Put off dance round piano

indicators.note: the dance word goes round the piano letter

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A dance around the piano is enough to deter anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive back or disgust someone.

clue.text: Many an afterthought about animals with tentacles

parts.note: POLY is the Greek-derived prefix meaning many
PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: Plenty of afterthoughts about tentacled creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Small aquatic creatures such as sea anemones and coral, tube-shaped with a ring of stinging arms.

clue.text: Swift brute

parts.note: in Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels, the brutish human-like creatures ruled by the horses

explanation.surface: A fast, savage beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' looks like 'fast', but it is the author Jonathan Swift.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse, loutish person, named after the degraded creatures in Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: One in a hundred-or just the opposite

definitions.text: One in a hundred-or just the opposite

indicators.note: flips 'one in a hundred' around, so the hundred is put inside the word one

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Something occurs one time in a hundred, or the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'One in a hundred' as written and it fails; 'or just the opposite' puts C inside ONE instead. The whole clue also hints at something happening a single time.
explanation.definitionFit: A single occasion, happening only one time.

clue.text: Criticise severely and take to pieces presumably

definitions.meaning: to slate a performance or piece of work
taken literally, to slice into bits

explanation.surface: Tearing someone's work apart, critically and literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically to savage in a review; literally to chop into pieces.

clue.text: Might he be troubled by heat burns?

definitions.text: Might he be troubled by heat burns?

indicators.note: the letters of these two words are troubled into a new order

explanation.surface: Could a person suffer from sunburn?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: someone lying in the sun could well suffer heat burns.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying out in strong sunshine to tan may get scorched.

clue.text: Don't worry, I'll have it when you've gone

definitions.text: Don't worry, I'll have it when you've gone

parts.words: Don't worry, I'll have it when you've gone
parts.note: a reassuring offer to deal with something, read as if bequeathing it in a will

explanation.surface: A helpful friend promising to sort something out.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means 'I'll handle it', but 'when you've gone' reads it as a bequest.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock phrase offering to take care of a job, also read as asking for a legacy.
